The entity IDs for the Tile integration have changed to reflect the human-friendly name of the Tile (as defined in the Tile mobile app). Please update your automations/etc. accordingly.

<!--
  You are amazing! Thanks for contributing to our project!
  Please, DO NOT DELETE ANY TEXT from this template! (unless instructed).
-->
## Proposed change
<!-- 
  Describe the big picture of your changes here to communicate to the
  maintainers why we should accept this pull request. If it fixes a bug
  or resolves a feature request, be sure to link to that issue in the
  additional information section.
-->
This PR adds a config flow for Tile. It also makes use of the more modern device tracker API under the hood.

I've tied this to `configuration.yaml` for now (except for a few deprecation notices) so that users can have a path to migrating to a config entry; I know ADR-0010 stipulates that we won't accept additions/alterations to YAML config in cases like this, but I believe this should be allowed so that there's a smoother transition.

## The problem
<!-- 
  Describe the issue you are experiencing here to communicate to the
  maintainers. Tell us what you were trying to do and what happened.
-->
ID is being stored as the Name field for [Tile integration](https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/tile/). 

## Environment
<!--
  Provide details about the versions you are using, which helps us to reproduce
  and find the issue quicker. Version information is found in the
  Home Assistant frontend: Developer tools -> Info.
-->

- Home Assistant Core release with the issue: 0.110.0
- Operating environment (Home Assistant/Supervised/Docker/venv): Supervised
- Integration causing this issue: [Tile integration](https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/tile/). 
- Link to integration documentation on our website: https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/tile/

## Problem-relevant `configuration.yaml`
<!--
  An example configuration that caused the problem for you. Fill this out even
  if it seems unimportant to you. Please be sure to remove personal information
  like passwords, private URLs and other credentials.
-->

```yaml
device_tracker:
  - platform: tile
    username: email@address.com
    password: MY_PASSWORD_123
```

## Traceback/Error logs
<!--
  If you come across any trace or error logs, please provide them.
-->

```txt

```

## Additional information

The tile device names are showing up as the device IDs.  The names are also not editable.
![Screen Shot 2020-05-20 at 8 55 45 PM](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/253367/82511841-58b59800-9adc-11ea-97d3-e4035a23b1d0.png)

It would be much better if the name could be pulled from the field "tile name".
![Screen Shot 2020-05-20 at 8 56 47 PM](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/253367/82511931-961a2580-9adc-11ea-80be-ffc566298696.png)

Hey there @bachya, mind taking a look at this issue as its been labeled with a integration (`tile`) you are listed as a [codeowner](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/dev/CODEOWNERS#L412) for? Thanks!
<sub><sup>(message by CodeOwnersMention)</sup></sub>

This is a feature request/alteration, not a bug report. That said, what you share is related to the `tile` integration's use of legacy device tracker functionality. I'm planning on updating it soon and will include this.

review_comments: Sorry, I got confused by your comment above on coverage. I see now.

Is this a breaking change?

Can we keep `async_setup_scanner` and import the config entry from there instead of adding new schema?

I'm not 100% sure it will work with a device tracker, but I was able to do something similar in `harmony` (remote.py) and `nut`(sensor.py) to avoid the need to avoid a breaking change.
I'm not terribly familiar with the legacy device tracker framework – is maintaining this method necessary for existing users of this platform?
I don't think so.  I'm suggesting importing the config entry here  (and having it otherwise do nothing) so they don't have to re-setup.

Bear with me – I'm wondering if this is necessary.

With this PR, `async_setup` inside `tile/__init__.py` imports the Tile config from`configuration.yaml`:

https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/368e46052edb5830a53bbb4e4b85008c5a3909ae/homeassistant/components/tile/__init__.py#L53-L68

This should do all the setup that's necessary, even for existing Tile consumers.

Am I missing something?

So if I setup tile https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/tile/
```
device_tracker:
 - platform: tile
   username: nick@koston.org
   password: SNIP
```

Its not going to be able to import the above since the schema is now 

```
tile:
   username: nick@koston.org
   password: SNIP
```

Okay, you were right – check out 3411f68.

That said, I still see a breaking change that I didn't previously: this PR updates the entity IDs to human-friendly strings; since this is the first time Tile makes use of the entity registry, they wouldn't have been in there before.
Does that mean we can drop the new CONFIG_SCHEMA as well?
